title: Exploratory Testing Plugin config
description: User/project configuration written by the setup skill. Contains references to secrets, never the secrets themselves.

schema_version.description: Bump when the structure changes so validate.py can detect and migrate old configs.

product.description: What is being tested. Used in prompts and report titles. Optional; detailed product knowledge belongs in 'sources', not here.

name.description: Product name as the team calls it, e.g. 'Acme Shop'.

description.description: One or two sentences: what the product is and who uses it.

sources.description: Where product knowledge lives. Any mix of types. Agents read each source's description to decide whether it helps with their task, and use sources read-only.

notes.description: Free-form notes about the setup, for people and for context. Information only: it never changes what agents may do, and it is not a place for settings the schema does not have.

name.description: Short identifier: lowercase letters, digits, underscores, hyphens.

secretRef.description: Pointer to a secret kept in the plugin's secrets file: 'secret:<NAME>'. NAME uses uppercase letters, digits and underscores, and should include the product name so projects sharing the file don't collide (e.g. secret:ACME_SHOP_STAGING_ADMIN_PW). Raw secrets are rejected by design.

role.description: Optional label such as admin, viewer, tester. Lets the orchestrator pick the right account when the environment lists several.

accounts.description: Who the tests log in as in this environment: a list of at least one account, or the word not_needed, meaning Claude does not log in (and asks the user if the app demands a login anyway). Required, so a forgotten login is never mistaken for 'no login needed'. With several accounts, use 'role' to tell them apart.

targets.description: What is tested in this environment. One or more; any mix of web, ios, android and api.

safety.description: What the skill may do in this environment. Required, so nobody gets permissive behavior by leaving it out. The rules each value brings are in the project's exploratory-testing/rules-of-engagement.md; the orchestrator copies the ones that apply into each run's engagement.md.

kind.description: test: data may be freely created, changed and deleted. prod_like: realistic or real data; create and change only data made during the run, no bulk deletes, don't touch existing records. production: observe only; no state-changing actions, ask before anything else.

allow_destructive.description: If false, never delete or overwrite existing data, whatever 'kind' says. Omitted means false. Cannot be true for 'production'.

allow_account_creation.description: Lets Claude sign up accounts through the app (for apps with self-registration, or to test sign-up). Omitted means Claude may not create accounts. Not allowed for 'production'. Registration uses only the address built from email_pattern.

email_pattern.description: Email address to register with. Exactly one {run} before the @, replaced by an id unique to each run, e.g. qa+{run}@acme-test.com. Use an address the team controls or a test domain that discards mail.

app_id.description: Bundle identifier (iOS) or package name (Android), e.g. com.acme.shop.staging.

build.description: Where the build under test comes from: a distribution channel, a prebuilt local file, or the project's own source code. Optional (e.g. when the app is already installed on the device).

devices.description: Preferred devices or simulators, e.g. 'iPhone 15 simulator', 'Pixel 8 emulator'.

apiTarget.description: A backend API tested directly, independent of any UI. Use one target per API if the environment has several.

spec.description: API specification (OpenAPI/Swagger file, GraphQL schema, .proto): a path relative to the project root, or an https URL.

description.description: What this API does and any quirks, in the user's words. Useful when an environment has several APIs.

apiAuth.description: How to authenticate against the API. These are service-level credentials, separate from the user logins in 'accounts'. Secrets are references only. Omitted means the API needs no authentication.

name.description: Header or query parameter name. Omitted means X-API-Key.

in.description: Where the key is sent. Omitted means header.

distributionBuild.description: A build downloaded from a distribution channel.

path.description: Path relative to the project root.

sourceBuild.description: Build the app from the source code of the project the skill is running in. Use the scheme/configuration/variant that produces this environment's build (e.g. a Staging scheme).

project_path.description: Xcode .xcworkspace/.xcodeproj, or the Gradle project directory, relative to the project root.

scheme.description: Xcode scheme that produces this environment's build, e.g. MyApp-Staging.

configuration.description: Xcode build configuration, e.g. Debug, Release, Staging.

command.description: Custom build command. Required when tool is 'other'; optional override for the other tools.

sourceDescription.description: What this source contains and when to use it, in the user's words. Claude reads it to decide which sources a task needs, e.g. 'Epics are features; NFRs are tagged nfr' or 'Architecture and supported-devices matrix. Not requirements.'

jql.description: Optional extra filter, e.g. for release scope.

path.description: Path relative to the project root.

otherSource.description: Any other system. Say in 'description' what it is and how to use it; if it is unclear how to reach it, agents ask the user.

description.description: What the tool is and how to reach it, in the user's words.
